jeonseChecklist.title: Jeonse Safety Checklist
jeonseChecklist.description: Check essential items before signing a jeonse lease and evaluate the risk level.
jeonseChecklist.dangerBannerDesc: Critical safety items are unchecked. Reconsider the contract and consult a professional.

items.ownerMatchDesc: If signed by proxy, verify power of attorney and seal certificate
items.noMortgageDesc: Risk increases if mortgage exceeds 60% of property value
items.noAuctionDesc: Check at the Supreme Court auction information site
items.taxPaidDesc: Request tax clearance certificate from landlord
items.landlordCreditDesc: If hard to verify directly, check if landlord owns multiple properties
items.multiProperty: Checked if landlord owns multiple properties
items.multiPropertyDesc: Multiple jeonse listings by same owner is a warning sign
items.actualVisitDesc: Personally verify property condition, defects, leaks
items.buildingConditionDesc: Check construction date; be cautious with buildings over 20 years old
items.neighborhoodCheckDesc: Compare jeonse-to-sale ratio on KB Real Estate or official transaction data
items.gapRatioDesc: Ratio above 80% indicates risk of underwater jeonse
items.specialConditionsDesc: Deposit return timing, restoration scope, early termination terms
items.moveInDate: Move-in and balance dates are clear
items.moveInDateDesc: Must register residence and get confirmation date on move-in day
items.realEstateAgentDesc: Verify agent registration on the national spatial information portal
items.depositInsuranceDesc: Check HUG/SGI/HF deposit insurance eligibility (most important!)
items.moveInReport: Planned to register residence + get confirmation date
items.moveInReportDesc: Register residence on move-in day (opposing power starts 00:00 the next day) + confirmation date (priority repayment)
items.priorityDepositDesc: Check small deposit priority limits (varies by region)

jeonseChecklist.riskCautionDesc: Some items are unchecked. Additional verification needed
jeonseChecklist.riskWarningDesc: Risk factors detected. Professional consultation recommended
jeonseChecklist.riskDangerDesc: Serious risk factors present. Reconsider the contract

whatIs.title: What is the Jeonse Safety Checklist?
whatIs.description: A systematic tool to check 20+ essential items before signing a jeonse lease. Covers registry verification, landlord credit, jeonse-to-sale ratio, deposit insurance eligibility, and calculates a risk score to help ensure a safe jeonse contract.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Enter property address and jeonse deposit amount
Go through 5 categories (registry, landlord, property, contract, insurance)
Mark each item as checked, unchecked, or not applicable
Risk score is automatically calculated as you check items
Save or share results for professional consultation

tips.title: Useful Tips
items: Deposit insurance (HUG) eligibility is the most important safety measure. HUG's return guarantee requires the deposit plus senior claims to be within 90% of the home price
Jeonse-to-sale ratio over 80% indicates high underwater risk

Opposing power starts at 00:00 the day after you take possession and register your residence. Add a clause that no mortgage will be set on the balance-payment day, and register plus get the confirmation date on move-in day
Re-check the registry on contract signing day (same-day changes possible)
Direct private deals without licensed agents require extra caution

items.a: Not legally required, but strongly recommended. If the landlord fails to return the deposit, the guarantor pays instead. Choose from HUG, SGI, or HF; HUG's return guarantee requires the deposit plus senior claims to be within 90% of the home price.
When the jeonse deposit approaches or exceeds the property's sale value. If the property goes to auction, you risk not recovering your deposit.

items.q: What's the difference between residence registration and confirmation date?
items.a: Residence registration (plus taking possession) gives you opposing power, effective from 00:00 the next day. The confirmation date is an official date stamp on your lease; together with opposing power it gives priority repayment ahead of junior creditors at auction. Get both on move-in day.
